title: CLEVER Benchmark Replication on Security-Extended Task Set

original_idea.body:
# CLEVER Benchmark Replication on Security-Extended Task Set

**Problem:** CLEVER (Curated Benchmark for Formally Verified Code Generation, arXiv 2505.13938) measures general correctness. Whether its evaluation methodology replicates on a set specifically augmented with security-critical tasks is untested.

**Direction:** Extend CLEVER by adding 30 security-relevant tasks. Run the CLEVER evaluation protocol on both the original and extended set. Measure whether security task performance is proportional to general performance (test for systematic security task penalty). Report results with the CLEVER leaderboard metrics.

**Why it matters:** If security tasks require special capabilities beyond general verified code generation, CLEVER and similar benchmarks systematically underweight security readiness. This replication with twist reveals whether security is a distinct capability dimension.

**Relevant context:** CLEVER (arXiv 2505.13938) is publicly available. The extension methodology is clearly defined. Security-specific formal verification remains underrepresented in all current benchmarks.
